Monocular depths, road edges, parked-car poses and residuals are model estimates. The modeled road ends before the visible bend and truck. Farther parking rows, the truck beyond the local patch, rear traffic, people near the distant building, and occluded spaces are excluded only under the explicit no-entry condition. Parking departures, door opening and new pedestrians entering the patch invalidate this prototype. No optimization, continuous collision verification or simulated prefix has been executed here.

premises.statement: Finite local prototype domain: the straight parking-access road and adjoining bay fronts within this polygon, with drivable pavement restricted to the separately supplied road polygon. Plan only along the present straight section for two seconds. All eight declared boundary vehicles are retained. Adopt no new unobserved entrant, no parking departure, no opening door and no pedestrian emerging into this domain during [0,2]. Farther truck/parking rows, rearward traffic outside x=-4, the bend and occluded building-side activity are not asserted absent; their entry is explicitly excluded by this conditional task. The blue boundary car is retained even though its center is beyond the intended route.

The declared cars are visually seated in parking bays, with no observed departure cue. Conditional short-term model: adopted mode holds each estimated pose fixed. Reasonable adverse mode permits center displacement of at most 0.15 m in any direction and yaw change at most 0.03 rad throughout [0,2], without doors opening. Both modes have absolute center speed at most 0.2 m/s. For the actual asynchronous side captures through t=0, assume these same parked conditions and speed bound: Nissan age 0.007616 s gives displacement <=0.001524 m; gray SUV age 0.042121 s gives displacement <=0.008425 m. Native reference centers equal the compensated evidence estimates, with those possible displacements included in alignment residuals. These are falsifiable stationary/settling hypotheses, not guarantees that parked vehicles cannot depart.

Assume ordinary passenger-car dimensions as natively specified, locally approximately level pavement, and no material road-edge change over two seconds. Use the visible left BMW's 4.7 m length and 1.85 m width as conditional size anchors. Perspective foreshortening, tire/base locations and the repeated parking-bay row establish approximate depth and lateral scale. The front image's curb lines define an approximately 7-8 m wide continuous access road; rear imagery supports pavement immediately behind the current footprint. The convex road polygon is a conservative straight-section estimate, not an extension into bays or the bend. Rear and side evidence is ego-compensated using the supplied acquisition history. Car envelopes are outward-rounded axis-aligned whole-body bounds; adverse envelopes additionally contain the full allowed settling displacement and yaw spread. Actor residuals are total model residuals and exclude neither alignment nor source error.

anchors.rationale: The individual dark BMW at the left bay front is consistent with an ordinary approximately 4.7 m passenger sedan; this is an assumed body size, not a measured specification.
An approximately 1.85 m sedan width supplies a second conditional dimension for this same visible actor and matches its native body hypothesis.

metric_scale_support.metric_reasoning: In the reference front image the left BMW occupies roughly the u=150-360 bay-front region, with its near tire/body base around v=650-670. A roughly perpendicular 4.7 m sedan at depth approximately 11 m is consistent with that projected extent after foreshortening. The camera's approximately 1266 px focal length fixes angular scale, while the assumed body dimensions and approximately level local pavement supply conditional metric depth. The white SUV and successive bay fronts on the right provide a consistency check on the resulting roughly 7-8 m curb-to-curb roadway. Calibration alone does not establish the pavement plane. The supplied polygon and actor positions therefore remain approximate model-metric hypotheses with explicit nonzero residuals.
